text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.58% today as oil prices climbed on escalating U.S.-Iran tensions in the Middle East. Reports of Iran launching a second undisclosed attack on U.S. Navy ships and tit-for-tat strikes over the weekend pushed crude toward a 6-week high, with world oil prices at $96.02 per barrel—up significantly from earlier in the week when the stock was trading lower.

The stock has recovered most of its losses from earlier this week, gaining 1.27% over two weeks as geopolitical risk to Middle East oil supplies has built a floor under energy prices. However, today's modest gain suggests the market is already pricing in most of the risk premium from these tensions; oil would need to climb substantially higher or the conflict would need to directly disrupt major production to drive a stronger rally for the company.
